WHO therefore rec- ommends the use of rifampicin and streptomycin or amikacin for 8 weeks.18 Consensus recommendations issued by practitioners in Victoria, Australia19 consider surgery to be the best treatment for Buruli ulcer, with antibacterial therapy being indicated for more extensive disease. Use of antibacterial may also possibly allow more conservative resection and reduce the risk of re- lapse. The recommended oral regimens were: at least 3 months of rifampicin given with clarithromycin, cipro- floxacin, or moxifloxacin. For more severe or extensive disease patients may also require intravenous amikacin for 4 to 8 weeks in addition to oral therapy. Reports of other therapies include a beneficial response with topi- cal nitrogen oxides in a small pilot study of 37 patients with Buruli ulcer,20 and healing after local application of phenytoin.21 Cutaneous disease due to M. haemophilum infection has been treated with an initial treatment course of rifabutin, ciprofloxacin, and clarithromycin, followed by clari- thromycin for 2 years.22 M. chelonae was successfully treated with clarithromycin and linezolid for one month, followed by a further 5 months of treatment with clari- thromycin.23 1.
